newsitem.title: UK: UK sales growth drops sharply in February - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK sales growth drops sharply in February - CBI.

text.p: British high street sales growth tumbled in February, the Confederation of British Industry said on Thursday.

The top industry organisation's latest distributive trades survey found 47 percent of retailers reported higher sales volumes last month compared with February last year, while 23 percent said sales had dropped -- a positive balance of only 24 percent.
In January, that balance was 36 percent and in February last year it was 30 percent.
The CBI said a slowing in sales growth since December meant the three monthly trend in sales was showing the smallest rise in sales volumes since May 1996.

"The slackening in the underlying trend continues and is consistent with mixed fortunes enjoyed by retailers, with only some sectors experiencing robust volume growth," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI's Distributive Trade Survey panel.

He said price competition is still fierce with retailers reporting the smallest annual increase in prices since August 1995. "With the downward pressure on prices set to continue, this survey provides good news for inflation."
Some 39 percent of retailers said average selling prices were higher than a year ago but 18 percent said they were lower.
In November a positive balance of 35 percent reported higher prices.
Clothing retailers and durable household goods stores reported little change in sales volumes compared with a year ago. The largest falls came from off licenses, footwear and leather stores.
Booksellers and stationers, grocers, confectioners, chemists and furniture and carpet retailers all saw marked sales growth in the year to February.
Wholesalers' sales volumes rose more than had been expected in February, but at a similar rate to January. Average selling prices moderated.

Motor traders' sales volumes picked up further in the year to February, the CBI said, posting the largest increase since August last year. Orders placed with suppliers also rose significantly for the first time in seven months.
